extra.reason: Superseded by epic postio-b9t (E1 — Foundations), which covers project setup as dep-linked tasks: toolchain install, cargo workspace, CI, CLAUDE.md, design tokens, fonts, app skeleton, Flatpak, bench harness.
Installed and verified: gtk4 4.22.4, libadwaita-1 1.9.3, webkitgtk-6.0 2.52.5, sqlite3 3.51.2, libsecret-1 0.21.7, glib-2.0 2.88.3. Versions and the dnf command are documented in CLAUDE.md.

Workspace created with all 9 crates; cargo build --workspace and cargo test --workspace both pass. Root Cargo.toml carries [workspace.package] and [workspace.dependencies] path entries. edition 2024, resolver 3.

CLAUDE.md rewritten with the TDD rule, build/test commands, verified system dep versions, the perf and motion budgets, the CI-enforced architectural invariants, design/scope decisions incl. canvas-wins keybindings, the architecture diagram, and the parallel-session claim protocol. AGENTS.md symlinked to it.

GO on io-imap; pin =0.6.0 (default-features=false + 'client'). All four open questions answered by source inspection; decision written to docs/decisions/0001-imap-library.md. (1) API churn: 0.5->0.6 changes only 3 files -- watch.rs, client.rs's watch_mailbox and lib.rs docs; everything we use is byte-identical, so adopt 0.6. Real risk is release velocity (6 minors in 11 weeks), mitigated by the existing MailBackend-only invariant. (2) QRESYNC/CONDSTORE ARE reachable: SelectParameter::{CondStore,QResync{..}}, FetchModifier::{ChangedSince,Vanished}, and ImapMailboxSelectData decodes highest_mod_seq + vanished_earlier + changed. E5's incremental sync design stands unchanged. Gaps: no UNCHANGEDSINCE on STORE, FETCH discards VANISHED (use SELECT QRESYNC instead), and watch::ImapMailboxWatch is unusable (whole-mailbox in-memory shadow). (3) Post-auth CAPABILITY re-read: yes via ImapSessionOpen/ImapClientStd::connect, which force ensure_capabilities=true; footgun is that the per-coroutine option defaults to false and returns an empty vec silently. (4) IDLE: exposed as its own coroutine with raw untagged events and an AtomicBool shutdown; timeout configurable in 0.6. iCloud caveats: omits the '* ENABLED' echo, has shipped malformed QRESYNC FETCH seq numbers, and io-imap silently skips undecodable untagged lines. Follow-ups filed as postio-wy2.1 through .4; postio-wy2.1 (live post-auth CAPABILITY assertion) is the one unverified assumption and is P1 before E4.2. No spike code written to the repo or workspace.

Added scripts/check-crate-boundaries.py: walks the resolved cargo metadata graph (normal+build deps transitively, plus the guarded crate's own dev-deps) and fails if postio-core reaches gtk4/libadwaita (or their -sys/gdk4/gsk4 companions) or postio-gtk reaches rusqlite/libsqlite3-sys/io-imap. Failure output names the offending crate, the offending dependency, the full path, and whether it is direct or transitive; a missing guarded crate is exit 2, not a silent pass. Package renames (postio-gtk uses gtk = {package = "gtk4"}) do not fool it. scripts/test-check-crate-boundaries.py builds throwaway path-only workspaces in a temp dir and proves the check fails for a direct gtk4 dep on postio-core, a transitive libadwaita dep, a direct rusqlite dep on postio-gtk, and an io-imap dev-dep - all 7 cases pass, no network, real manifests untouched. Both are wired into the CI 'Crate boundaries' job. Check is green on the current tree.

Added .github/workflows/ci.yml with four jobs: fmt (cargo fmt --all --check), boundaries (crate-boundary check + its self-test + a guard asserting no workflow opts into the ignored live-server tests), build (apt-installs libgtk-4-dev, libadwaita-1-dev, libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev, libsqlite3-dev, libsecret-1-dev, libglib2.0-dev, libpango1.0-dev, then clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test --workspace), and bench (detects bench targets via cargo metadata and skips cleanly while none exist, so the criterion harness bead can land with no workflow change). Cargo registry and target dir cached via actions/cache keyed on Cargo.lock. Compiling jobs run on ubuntu-26.04 because postio-gtk pins gtk4 v4_20 / libadwaita v1_7 / pango v1_56, which ubuntu-24.04 (GTK 4.14, libadwaita 1.5) cannot satisfy; resolute ships 4.22.2/1.9.1/1.57, matching the dev box. All package names verified against packages.ubuntu.com. Gate behaviour verified locally: fmt drift exits 1 and clippy -D warnings fails the build on a scratch crate; the boundary job is green. Note the workspace itself is not green right now - rustfmt drift (filed as postio-nwp) and in-flight TDD compile errors in postio-imap tests - both owned by other agents, not by this CI config.

Implemented pure domain types in crates/postio-model (test-first): newtype ids (AccountId/IdentityId/MailboxId/MessageId/ThreadId/AttachmentId/ContactId/LabelId/DraftId + Uid/UidValidity/ModSeq/BlobId/RfcMessageId), Account/Identity/ServerConfig/Signature, Mailbox with MailboxRole special-use resolution (handles iCloud 'Sent Messages'/'Deleted Messages'), Message with every spec.md §4 field incl. ServerIdentifiers and LocalSyncState/BodyState, Thread, Attachment, Contact, Flag/FlagSet, Label, Draft, Headers, EmailAddress, normalize_subject. 32 tests across tests/invariants.rs, tests/serde_roundtrip.rs, tests/purity.rs and subject unit tests; clippy -D warnings clean. Crate depends only on serde+chrono; no storage or protocol crate.

Implemented the config.toml schema and typed deserialization in crates/postio-config: [ui] [keys] [accounts] [sync] [filters] as documented typed structs with defaults; missing/empty file yields working defaults; unknown keys round-trip via a per-section extras passthrough; secret-bearing keys are stripped on parse AND on serialize and parser errors are redacted, so no password can reach disk; accounts reference a keyring entry (postio:<id>:imap|smtp). 51 tests (schema.rs, secrets.rs, unit + doctests) all pass; cargo clippy -D warnings clean.

Keyring credential storage landed in crates/postio-imap/src/secret.rs, test-first. All three acceptance criteria met: (1) password round-trips and survives a restart, and a live canary test proves it never reaches disk in cleartext — plaintext is structurally impossible since Password is not Serialize and SecretSource has no raw variant (hand-written Deserialize, because serde deny_unknown_fields does not bite on internally-tagged enums); (2) a locked keyring yields SecretError::Locked with unlock instructions, never a panic; (3) Flatpak works by construction via oo7's portal path, empirically unverified until a manifest exists — follow-up postio-64h. Also ships the himalaya-style 'run a command' escape hatch, read-only. 22 unit/integration tests plus 2 #[ignore] live ones, all green against the real GNOME Secret Service; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.

Autoconfig probe landed in crates/postio-imap/src/discovery/, test-first, built on io-pim-discovery 0.7 as the bead note directed. All three acceptance criteria met: (1) an iCloud address resolves from the builtin table with requires_app_password and an appleid.apple.com note, without touching the network at all — the test's transport panics if reached; (2) a domain with no autoconfig walks the four probes and falls to DiscoveryOutcome::ManualEntry rather than erroring or guessing at the user; (3) probing is cancellable and fully unit-tested against a mocked transport — 14 integration tests plus 12 unit tests, zero network, with the live probe #[ignore]. Cancellation, per-step timeout and whole-probe deadline all covered by tests that assert the probe returns promptly. clippy -D warnings and fmt clean; the #[ignore] live probe was run once by hand and resolves gmail.com through the real chain.

Command/CommandId/MessageTarget, Context/ContextSet, Event and the enumerable command registry landed in postio-core (command.rs, context.rs, event.rs, registry.rs). 30 commands, each with a stable snake_case id, human title, default binding and context set; ids and defaults verified against postio-config DEFAULT_BINDINGS by test. Destructive commands carry a Recovery (Undo/Confirm), enforced by test. 29 tests + doctest pass; clippy -D warnings clean; scripts/check-crate-boundaries.py passes (no GTK).

Pure, total query parser in crates/postio-search: parse(&str, NaiveDate) -> ParsedQuery. All canvas operators (from/to/subject/has:attach/is:unread/is:flagged/before/after/in/filename/larger, plus smaller and list) compose with each other and with free text; negation via leading -; quoted phrases; ISO/loose (aug1)/relative (yesterday, last week, 3m) dates; K/M/G sizes. Half-typed input never errors — unusable operator values become Partial tokens and unknown operators degrade to free text. Output separates filters from free text and offers an FTS5 MATCH expression; every token carries a byte span and raw text for the chip UI. 90 tests (67 acceptance incl. an all-prefixes test and a 4000-case fuzz, 22 unit, 1 doctest); clippy -D warnings clean.

Migration 0001 creates all 13 spec.md §6 tables (+contacts), with indexes for the message-list (mailbox_id, received_at DESC, id DESC), thread lookup, Message-ID, UID and QRESYNC. Forward-only numbered runner in postio-storage::migrations: each migration in its own transaction with the schema_migrations row and PRAGMA user_version, FNV-1a checksums rejecting edits to applied migrations, SchemaTooNew guard, ordering guard. 45 tests (4 unit, 29 migration-contract, 10 model-fidelity, 2 doc), clippy -D warnings clean. Bodies/attachment bytes stay out of SQLite: blob-id columns only, asserted by test. sync_state holds per-mailbox uid_validity/uid_next/highest_mod_seq, tested atomic with message writes.

Added src/validate.rs (positioned, plain-language errors + validity line with parse timing), src/source.rs (dotted key -> line/column via toml's spanned DeTable), src/live.rs (LiveConfig keeps last-good on a bad edit), and keys::binding_problem for binding syntax. 37 new tests in tests/validate.rs, tests/live.rs and unit tests; validation of a normal config runs in well under the advertised 2 ms; validation errors are redacted and a secret in the file is reported as a fix-me without quoting its value.

build.rs parses the :root block of Design/_ds/industry-*/styles.css and generates crates/postio-gtk/data/tokens.css: raw tokens verbatim as --postio-*, semantic roles, and the libadwaita named colours overridden per scheme. Light in :root, dark in :root.postio-dark (neutral-900 ground, accent-900 selection, accent-400 steel, hairlines lift to neutral-700), high contrast in :root.postio-hc — GTK 4.22 ignores @media prefers-color-scheme in an app provider, so crate::style syncs the classes with AdwStyleManager. Wireframe chrome (corner marks, transparent line-drawing cards) deliberately not ported. Tests: tokens.rs proves reproducibility (CI fails on a stale file), propagation from a retuned source, GTK-subset safety and no wireframe chrome; gtk_style.rs loads the sheet through GtkCssProvider (zero parse errors) and resolves every token in all four scheme combinations.

38 .eml fixtures in crates/postio-model/tests/corpus/ (all invented, RFC 2606 domains) plus a one-call loader in postio-model::test_corpus behind the off-by-default 'test-corpus' feature: load()/get()/all()/names()/by_category()/by_categories() over 23 category tags. Covers plain text, format=flowed, HTML newsletter with tables+inline CSS, tracking pixel and remote images, multipart alternative/mixed/related and 3-level nesting, cid: inline images incl. a dangling ref, a 256 KiB attachment, RFC 2231 filenames, ISO-8859-1 / Shift_JIS / UTF-7 / mislabeled windows-1252 / UTF-8 emoji+RTL, base64 and quoted-printable, RFC 2047 encoded words correct and broken, malformed headers, bare-LF, truncated multipart, missing Message-ID/Date, duplicate Message-ID, broken References, a 7-message List-Id thread with three distinct half-linked replies for JWZ, PGP signed and encrypted, a delivery-status bounce and a calendar invite. 20 acceptance tests in tests/corpus_loader.rs prove the loader reads every fixture byte-for-byte, that the table/disk/README stay in sync, that category coverage minimums hold, and that no real personal data or non-reserved domain appears. Verified an out-of-workspace crate can consume it. Loader returns raw bytes, not parsed messages, since MIME parsing is postio-8gk; follow-up filed as postio-tn9.1.

Barlow (Regular/Medium/Bold/Italic), Barlow Condensed (Regular/SemiBold) and IBM Plex Mono (Regular/Medium) vendored from google/fonts under the OFL into crates/postio-gtk/data/fonts/, each family next to its OFL.txt, provenance recorded in postio.gresource.xml. All eight faces plus the three licences are compiled into the GResource bundle by build.rs and linked into the binary. postio_gtk::fonts::install() unpacks them from the bundle into a content-addressed cache dir (Pango only takes a path) and registers them with pango_font_map_add_font_file on the default font map; fonts::licenses() exposes the OFL text for attribution. No network, no system installation. tokens.css sets the roles: Barlow Condensed for .postio-heading/.postio-title/.postio-kicker, Barlow as the inherited body face, IBM Plex Mono for .postio-mono/.postio-count/.postio-meta/.postio-key. The gtk_style test verifies on this box — which has none of the three installed — that CSS font-family resolves to each embedded family and that the condensed face really is narrower.

Added src/watch.rs: ConfigWatcher watches the config file's DIRECTORY with notify (so editor write-then-rename and first-run file creation are both seen), filters events down to the one file, ignores Access events (our own reload opens the file, which would otherwise feed the watcher forever), debounces a burst into exactly one reload, and reparses+validates on its own thread, handing over a Checked for LiveConfig::apply on the UI thread — the seam postio-o04 can diff on. Debounce is a pure state machine over an injected Instant, so the coalescing rule is unit-tested with no sleeps; 11 integration tests cover save, burst, atomic rename (twice), create, delete, invalid edit keeping last-good, scratch files, and drop. Added ConfigError::Watch (notify kept out of the public API). Dep: notify 8.2 added to crates/postio-config/Cargo.toml only.
Resolved during the wave: each agent ran cargo fmt on its own crate, so 'cargo fmt --all --check' is now clean across the workspace. Verified after all seven agents completed.
